newsitem.title: CHINA: China to order 180 new planes to 2000 - official.
newsitem.headline: China to order 180 new planes to 2000 - official.

text.p: China was expected to place orders for about 180 new civilian planes through the year 2000, a senior aviation official said.

About 240 civilian aircraft, including those already on order but not yet delivered, were expected to enter into service over the period to meet the needs of China's fast growing aviation industry, said Shen Yuankang, vice-minister of the General Administration of Civil Aviation of China.
Shen, speaking in a recent interview, declined to give a dollar figure for the planes or say how many would be built by U.S. or European manufacturers.
The bulk of the new planes would be 150- to 200-seaters, Shen said, adding that he expected a growing market for 100-seaters after 2000 due to their low operating costs.
About 80 civilian planes were expected to be retired between 1996 and 2000, he said.
China had 416 planes as of the end of 1995, more than 40 percent of which were U.S.-made and over 20 percent European-made, Shen said. The rest were Russian.
China's civil aviation sector has expanded rapidly in the past 15 years, growing by an annual average of 20.6 percent between 1980 and 1995.
The industry was forecast to grow by an average of 14 percent annually over the next five years, Shen said.
Passenger volume and the total of cargo handled by airlines was expected to double to 100 million passengers and 2.36 million tonnes by the year 2000, he said.
China ranked seventh in the world last year in terms of total passenger volume compared with 33rd in 1980, Shen said. In terms of cargo handled, China ranked 11th in 1995 compared with 35th in 1980.
